hold.description: Ontology-owned hold, written only by actions. Task references are authoritative; times of application come from the trusted action clock.
hold.title: effect

task.description: Reference to the task owning this object.

effect.description: Change blocked by this hold; unique among active holds on the task.

until.description: Condition that must be satisfied before lifting this hold; free text, not an expiry timestamp.

status.description: Current hold status; allowed values are declared by its value type.

lift_reason.description: Optional explanation of why the hold condition was satisfied.

intent.description: Kept for a hold written before version 24 (set_hold_on); set by no action, and such a hold stops nothing.

decision.description: Ontology-owned decision, written only by actions. Task references are authoritative; times of application come from the trusted action clock.

task.description: Reference to the task owning this object.

topic.description: Short topic name; only one decision per task and topic is current. Reuse it when replacing that decision.

reason.description: Optional explanation of why this decision was made.

undo.description: Optional instructions for reversing the decision.

status.description: Current decision status; allowed values are declared by its value type.

supersedes.description: Reference to the previous decision replaced by this current decision.

decided_at.description: Trusted UTC application time when this decision was recorded; generated by $now.

triage.description: Set once by triage_decision on a row of the user.

kpi.description: Reference to the KPI object whose measurement is being recorded.

value.description: Measured value as text, required for each measurement.

observed_at.description: When the value was observed, as normalized UTC ISO 8601 text, for example 2026-11-11T00:00:00Z; distinct from recording time.

evidence.description: Path or command whose output proves the measured value; do not include private payloads.

recorded_at.description: Trusted UTC application time when the measurement was recorded; generated by $now.

task.description: Reference to the task owning this object.

tier.description: Worker judgment level: mechanical, bounded, open or review.

runtime.description: CLI or executor used by this worker run, for example codex.

session.description: Optional runtime session identifier for locating the worker session; not an authenticated identity.

started_at.description: Trusted UTC application time when the worker run started; generated by $now.

status.description: Current worker_run status; allowed values are declared by its value type.

result.description: Final worker outcome supplied when closing; separate from last_note progress.

closed_at.description: Trusted UTC application time when the worker run closed; generated by $now.

last_note.description: Current worker progress; stored separately from the final result.

running_in.description: Set only by the start action while running; cleared by the close action for duplicate checks.

memory_record.description: Cross-task retrieval index only. Git memory/records files own content and provenance; actions own publication status.

document_id.description: Server retrieval document id; equal to the stable Git record id used as this object native key.

status.description: Publication state; never copied into the Git original.

supersedes.description: Optional predecessor replaced by this record; distinct successors retain their own stable identity.

body_hash.description: SHA-256 of the exact selected UTF-8 original file bytes; computed outside that file.

plan.description: One plan per thread. Opening estimates are immutable through actions; amending current_lines clears scope_reviewed.

thread.description: One task/key work thread with a consumer kind and first observed use; amendments retain prior values in object history.
thread.title: key

review.description: Ontology-owned review of one head by one model, written only by actions.

running_in.description: Set only by the start action while running; cleared by the close action for duplicate checks.

unit.description: The unit whose page (kind page) or head (kind packet) is reviewed; such a review closes with close_unit_review.

intent.description: The intent whose plan is reviewed (kind plan).

round.description: The verifier's round on the unit.

carried_from.description: The accepting review carry_review carried to this head; its other members are read there.

install.description: Ontology-owned record of one install attempt on one installed file, written only by actions: started before an installer runs, closed after a read of the target.
install.title: commit

target.description: The installed file the attempt changes.

repository.description: owner/name of the repository of the commit.

commit.description: The commit the attempt installs, or rolls back to.

attempt.description: 1 for the first attempt on this target and commit.

from.description: What a read of the target showed before the attempt.

from_sha256.description: The digest of the target file before: the name of the copy the installer keeps is made of it.

by.description: Who ran it: a timer's invocation or a Lead's session.

head.description: The accepted head whose merge is the commit.

reviews.description: Every accepting review of the installed range.

past.description: Commits a Lead stepped over, 40 hex each, joined by one space.

running_in.description: Set only by the start action while running; cleared by the close action for the duplicate check.

to.description: What the read after the installers showed.

rollback_binary.description: The copy of the file that the installer kept.

rollback_content.description: The tarball of the content that the installer kept.

rolls_back.description: For kind rollback: the attempt whose install it undoes.

objective.description: Ontology-owned objective of a task: a checkable sentence the user's row is the source of, written only by actions; restated in place (history and action log keep earlier sentences).
objective.title: name

check.description: Command whose exit 0 shows the objective holds; absent: unmeasured.

source.description: Current row of the user with words when stated or restated.

confirmed_by.description: Row of the user, later than stated_at; cleared by restate.

confirmed_at.description: Kept after a restate (a scalar cannot be cleared); valid only while status is confirmed.

item.description: Ontology-owned entry of a task's backlog, written only by actions.
item.title: key

key.description: Unique per task for ever: the handle a unit request names.

first_use.description: Who uses the result first and the run that shows it.

repository.description: owner/name; set by start_item for a unit, kept after a release (a scalar cannot be cleared).

review.description: The accepting review that closed a unit.

evidence.description: Command and output that closed work without a pull request.

board.description: Ontology-owned order of one task's items; key: the task's key. The first set_order creates it (the opt-in of a task).
board.title: task

order.description: Items in order; elements are not checked by the store.

request.description: One message of the user that orders, decides, prefers, corrects, stops, answers or delegates, in the user's own words. Record it with record_request, then route it to an intent or set it aside; correct it with supersede_request.
request.title: topic

words.description: The user's own text in the user's language, unchanged. No action changes it: a correction is a new request (supersede_request).

words_verified.description: True when a program read the words from a session record; false when an agent wrote them otherwise. Set once: verified words replace unverified ones only through supersede_request.

truncated.description: True when the words were cut to fit 24,000 bytes; the record holds the whole message.

record.description: The session record the words were read from (a path, with a line or id), so a reader can check them.

reading.description: What the agent took the message to mean, in English: the order, decision or answer in a sentence or two.

kind.description: order, decision, preference, correction, stop, answer, or delegation: the user hands the confirmation of named intents to the Lead for a time the user does not step in.

topic.description: A short label that groups related requests (view requests_by_topic); not unique.

said_at.description: When the user said it, UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ); never later than the time of recording.

recorded_at.description: When the request was recorded, from the action clock.

session.description: The session in which the user said it.

runtime.description: The CLI that held the session, such as claude or codex.

status.description: current, or superseded: replaced by a correction (supersede_request) or ended by the user (end_delegation).

route.description: unrouted (not handled yet), subject (about the subject named by subject), aside (part of no intent; route_reason says why); intent, unit and finding were written before version 24.

intent.description: The intent the request is part of while route is intent; cleared by set_request_aside.

route_reason.description: Why the request was set aside. Valid only while route is aside: no rule clears a scalar, so the reason of an earlier aside stays after a later route.

routed_at.description: When the request was last routed or set aside.

legacy_decision.description: The user's decision row of version 9 this request was carried from (ontology/migrate).

unit.description: Kept for a request written before version 24 (route unit); set by no action.

finding.description: Kept for a request written before version 24 (route finding); set by no action.

subject.description: What the request is about while route is subject (route_request); cleared by set_request_aside.

intent.description: One objective of the user, keyed by a short name. Draft it from the request that started it, add criteria, have the user confirm it, check the criteria, then close it met or retire it.

outcome.description: What is true when the intent is met, as sentences that can each be checked true or false.

why.description: Why the user wants it: the need behind the outcome.

first_user.description: Who or what uses the result first, and the real run that shows it working.

not_included.description: What the user does not want done under this intent.

constraints.description: Limits the work keeps: tools, data, cost, time, places not to touch.

questions.description: Open questions to the user, at most five: each with the default the Lead assumes until the user answers, and the answer (empty until answered). Given whole; replaces the list.

origin.description: The request that started the intent.

status.description: draft (being written), assumed (the Lead proceeds unconfirmed), confirmed (by the user's word or a delegation), met (closed with its criteria passed) or retired.

amended_at.description: Time of draft_intent or of the last amend_intent: a confirming request is said later.

confirmed_by.description: The request that confirmed the intent: the user's word, or a delegation when confirmed_delegated is true. Cleared by amend_intent.

confirmed_at.description: When it was confirmed. Valid only while status is confirmed or met: it cannot be cleared and stays after an amendment.

confirmed_delegated.description: True when the Lead confirmed it under a delegation of the user, not by the user's own word.

assumed_reason.description: Why the Lead proceeds without the user's confirmation. Valid only while status is assumed.

lead_session.description: The session that leads the work of this intent.

lead_named_by.description: The user's request that named the Lead.

directory.description: The task directory of the work for this intent.

notes.description: The Lead's free text for the next Lead: the state, the next step, where things are. Replaced whole by note_intent.

closed_at.description: When the intent was closed met or retired.

closed_reason.description: Why it was closed: how the outcome was shown, or why it was retired.

principles.description: The principles the intent obeys; set whole by set_intent_principles.

principle.description: A want of the user that outlives one intent: a pillar, or a want under one. Record it from the requests that state it; an intent names the principles it obeys.

order_key.description: The place in the hierarchy: two-digit segments joined by a dot, such as 01 for a pillar and 01.02 for a want under it. The engine orders it as a string and does not check the form.

statement.description: The want, in the user's sense.

parent.description: The pillar or want this one is under; none for a pillar.

status.description: current, or retired when the user no longer wants it.

amended_at.description: Time of record_principle or of the last amend_principle.

criterion.description: One success criterion of an intent: a statement checkable true or false and how to check it. An intent is confirmed only with one that is not waived, and closed only when none is open or failed.
criterion.title: statement

intent.description: The intent this criterion belongs to.

statement.description: What must be true, checkable as true or false.

check.description: How to check it: the command, the test, the eval with its threshold, or the real run to observe.

baseline.description: For a number: its value before the work, with its source and time.

state.description: open (not checked yet), pass, fail, or waived by the user.

evidence.description: What showed the state: the command and its result, or the reason of a waiver.

checked_at.description: When check_criterion last set the state.

waived_by.description: The user's request that waived the criterion.

unit.description: One piece of work that ends alone (for code: one pull request), keyed by a short name. Its properties are its page (add_unit, amend_unit) and its state (the other unit actions).

lane.description: small (one request of the user, one repository, class plain) or objective (part of an open intent). Never changes.

class.description: plain; contract or effect: a page review before ready, and the Lead's approval of the head before the merge or close.

intent.description: The intent the unit serves; required in the lane objective. Never changes.

origin.description: The current request the unit answers; required in the lane small. Never changes.

objective.description: The state after the merge, as sentences that can each be checked true or false.

interface.description: What the Lead fixes: names, forms and answers the worker keeps.

invariants.description: What must stay true while the unit changes things.

acceptance.description: The checks: a command and its kind, fails_on_base (fails before the change) or invariant (holds before and after).

not_built.description: What the unit must not build.

write_set.description: The paths the unit may change (globs).

read_first.description: The files the worker reads before any effect.

specs.description: The design sources the unit implements.

report.description: What the worker's report must hold.

repository.description: owner/name; absent for a document, a measurement or an effect on the host.

branch.description: The branch of the unit's pull request.

implementer.description: Runtime, model and effort of the implementer.

verifier.description: Runtime, model and effort of the verifier.

depends_on.description: Units that must be merged or done before this one starts.

clauses.description: The sentences of the specifications the page names.

wave.description: The Lead's number of the wave the unit belongs to.

page_digest.description: The digest of the page as add_unit or amend_unit left it.

state.description: draft, ready, running, accepted, stopped, merged, done (ended without a repository) or dropped.

amended_at.description: Time of add_unit or of the last amend_unit: a review of the page or of a head counts only when it started later.

ended_at.description: When the unit stopped, merged, was closed done or dropped.

pull_request.description: The number of the unit's pull request.

head.description: The head under review: a commit, or for a unit without a repository the SHA-256 of its evidence.

approved_head.description: The head the Lead approved (approve_unit). Valid only while it equals head.

rounds.description: Verifier rounds so far: 0 from add_unit; the caller of record_head passes the new number.

writers.description: The sessions that wrote to the unit's branch, empty from add_unit on; none of them closes a review of the unit.

stop_cause.description: Why the unit stopped, a short code. Valid only while state is stopped.

stop_detail.description: The stop in words. Valid only while state is stopped.

waits_on.description: The constraint a ready unit waits on, as the dispatch pass last saw it.

evidence.description: What shows a unit without a pull request is done; its SHA-256 is the head.

run.description: One stage of one agent: who ran, on what, how long, how many tokens. start_run, then close_run.

unit.description: The unit the run worked on.

intent.description: The intent the run worked on, for a stage outside a unit.

role.description: The stage: lead, implementer, verifier, reviewer, dispatch.

runtime.description: The CLI that ran, such as claude or codex.

state.description: The end state the run record names.

served_by.description: The model that served, when it differs from model.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens not read from the cache.

cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the cache.

limit.description: The usage-limit reading as the run record holds it.

stream.description: The raw stream of the run.

running_in.description: The unit while the run is running; cleared by close_run.

finding.description: Something that should change the system, keyed by its detector and signature. Open it, see it again, plan it into a unit or an intent, dismiss or close it.

kind.description: incident, lesson, drift, security, note or bottleneck.

detector.description: What found it: a check, a command or an agent's role.

summary.description: What should change, in a sentence or two.

evidence.description: The last evidence: output, a path and line, a record.

severity.description: info, act (plan it) or urgent (act now).

state.description: open, planned (into a unit or an intent), dismissed or closed.

last_seen_at.description: When it was last opened, seen again or reopened.

unit.description: The unit it was planned into.

intent.description: The intent it was planned into.

subject.description: What the finding is about (open_finding, see_finding_again, reopen_finding); may name no object.

reason.description: Why it was dismissed or closed.

ended_at.description: When it was dismissed or closed.

repository.description: owner/name of the repository; no value for the shared instructions.

path.description: The file's path in the repository, or its absolute path for the shared instructions.

heading.description: The heading path, parent headings joined by ' > '; the file's name for the text above its first heading.

first_line.description: The first line of the section (its heading line), counted from 1.

last_line.description: The last line before the next heading of the same or a higher level, or the file's last line.

commit.description: The last commit at origin/main that changed the file; no value for the shared instructions.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the file's bytes when it was indexed.

text.description: The words of the section's lines, each run of white space one space, at most 4,000 bytes cut at a character boundary.

path.description: The file's path in the repository.

rule.description: R and the number of the sentence.

commit.description: The last commit at origin/main that changed the file.

line.description: The sentence's first line, counted from 1.

tests_total.description: How many citations of the sentence the repository holds.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the sentence's lines joined by line feeds.

text.description: The words of the sentence's lines, each run of white space one space.

tests.description: The first 100 citations, path:line, by path then line.

host.description: A tailnet node that runs work: local, the host of the store; a key of the policy's hosts; or a node a Lead declares. Its machine groups the nodes of one computer.

account.description: An account of a runtime, keyed by the last path component of its directory: the allowance its newest run reports, or one the user states (specs/ap/resource.md).

task.description: Reference to the task owning the new object.

effect.description: Change blocked by this hold; unique among active holds on the task.

until.description: Condition that must be satisfied before lifting this hold; free text, not an expiry timestamp.

scope.description: What the hold covers, in words.

task.description: Reference to the task owning the new object.

topic.description: Short topic name; only one decision per task and topic is current. Reuse it when replacing that decision.

text.description: The decision being made; state the chosen behavior concretely.

decided_by.description: Who made the decision: user or lead. This is attribution, not authentication.

reason.description: Optional explanation of why this decision was made.

undo.description: Optional instructions for reversing the decision.

Use supersede_decision with the current decision reference for this topic.

text.description: The decision being made; state the chosen behavior concretely.

decided_by.description: Who made the decision: user or lead. This is attribution, not authentication.

reason.description: Optional explanation of why this decision was made.

undo.description: Optional instructions for reversing the decision.

submission_criteria.message: Read decision and choose one whose status is current.
User attribution requires quoted user_words and user_form.
Record the Lead decision and quote the user question in its reason.

define_kpi.description: Define a KPI: task identifies its task, name is unique there, definition states what is counted and from which source, and target is the desired value. Actions take the full Id from search; view arguments take the native key.
